name: @fossil-lang/corpus
description: Open a fossil corpus and read it. `openCorpus` is the door: it runs the fossil-graph verb surface as verb→SQL in WASM (fossil-graph-wasm) and delegates execution to a host-provided DuckDB-WASM query callback (e.g. keasy's Mosaic coordinator) — the larger-than-RAM query layer for whatever draws the graph; fossil ships no viewer. The `./address` subpath publishes the addressing alone: resolveCorpus turns a GraphAr manifest into tile URLs, synchronously and without WASM.
//name: This was `@fossil-lang/graph` and it does not draw one. Its door is `openCorpus`, every type it exports is `Corpus*`, and the package that DOES put vertices on a GPU — `@kanzo-tech/graph` — sits beside it in `apps/playground/package.json`, where two entries called `graph` meant nothing about an import told you which. The Rust crates behind it are deliberately NOT renamed: `fossil-graph` is a verb surface over a property graph, which is what it says it is, and a cargo name is not in the import space this collision happened in. See /docs/design/corpus.
//exports: TWO entries, and there were three. `.` is the door: `openCorpus`, the camera and the six verbs, and it needs the WASM — `corpus.js` reaches `client.js` and `load.js`, both of which static-import `../pkg/fossil_graph_wasm.js`, so a consumer without that build output cannot load the barrel at all. `./corpus` was a third entry whose ONE justification was that its closure reached no WASM; the door reaches the verbs now, so the justification is gone and the subpath with it. `./address` stays, and it is the one that genuinely stands alone: its closure is `address.js` + `manifest.js` and nothing else — synchronous, WASM-free, no `query` callback, and it is the published arithmetic a third-party reader would otherwise re-derive. That is not a claim in a comment: `tests/address-standalone.test.ts` compiles the closure into a package directory with no `pkg/` in it and imports the subpath from a child Node process.

scripts.build: pnpm run build:wasm && pnpm run gen:types && tsc -p tsconfig.json
